source_meta._title: Posed mannequins don't use the correct hitbox

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.21.9 Pre-Release 1 in a fresh single-player Creative-mode world with commands enabled, using keyboard and mouse controls.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected version, 1.21.9 Pre-Release 1. Do not use the listed fix version, 1.21.9 Pre-Release 2.
Use a world in which the player can execute commands. A fresh Creative-mode single-player world is recommended because the report does not specify a game mode or server requirement.
Use a fresh world or otherwise ensure there are no pre-existing minecraft:mannequin entities near the player; the supplied @n selector must resolve to the mannequin created during this procedure.
The client must be able to display Java Edition entity hitboxes with the F3+B debug shortcut. On keyboards that assign media functions to the function-key row, Fn may also need to be held.
No world seed, coordinates, dimension, difficulty, graphics setting, datapack, resource pack, or multiplayer configuration is specified by the report.

steps.action: Start Minecraft: Java Edition using the launcher installation configured for 1.21.9 Pre-Release 1. At the main menu, verify that the displayed version is exactly 1.21.9 Pre-Release 1 before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and identifies the running version as 1.21.9 Pre-Release 1.

steps.action: From the main menu, select Singleplayer, then Create New World. Set Game Mode to Creative, ensure commands are allowed, and create the world. Creative mode is an execution convenience rather than a report-stated requirement.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Allow Commands: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a newly created Creative-mode world and can open chat.

steps.action: Do not execute the reproduction commands while the world is still loading. Wait until the terrain around the player has rendered and movement and camera controls respond normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, the loading overlay is gone, and the player can move and look around without waiting for chunks to appear.

steps.action: Move to a clear, well-lit area with enough open space to see a human-sized entity from several blocks away. Confirm that no other mannequins are present nearby so the later nearest-entity selector is unambiguous.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in an open viewing area and there are no pre-existing mannequins nearby.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the report's mannequin summon command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds and one mannequin appears at the command execution position near or overlapping the player.

steps.action: Move approximately three blocks away from the summoned mannequin, then turn the camera toward it. Position the camera so the mannequin's entire body is visible from head to feet; do not summon any additional mannequins.
steps.exact_input: Hold S or another movement key until approximately 3 blocks away, then aim the crosshair toward the mannequin
steps.success_cue: Exactly one mannequin is visible, its whole body fits on screen, and the player is no longer occupying the same position as it.

steps.action: Enable entity-hitbox rendering by holding F3 and pressing B once. If the keyboard uses the function-key row for media controls, hold Fn together with F3 while pressing B. Release the keys after the toggle occurs.
steps.exact_input: F3+B (or Fn+F3+B when required by the keyboard)
steps.success_cue: A debug confirmation such as "Entity hitboxes: shown" appears, and a white hitbox outline is rendered around the mannequin.

steps.action: With the mannequin still visible and hitbox rendering enabled, press T to open chat. Enter the report's pose-modification command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Because this is the only nearby mannequin, @n[type=minecraft:mannequin] should select it.
steps.exact_input: /data modify entity @n[type=minecraft:mannequin] pose set value crouching
steps.success_cue: The command reports successful modification of the selected entity's data, the mannequin model has adopted the crouching pose, and hitbox rendering remains enabled.

stor.handoff_condition: The only nearby mannequin has just been changed to the crouching pose with the report's exact /data command. The mannequin's full model is in view, entity-hitbox rendering is enabled, and no additional action has been taken since the command completed. Begin hitbox observation now.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, coordinates, dimension, or server configuration. This plan uses a fresh Creative-mode single-player world as the simplest way to provide command permission without adding unrelated setup.

The description also identifies swimming and fall_flying as affected poses, but the report supplies an exact pose-modification command only for crouching. Following the simplest deterministic reproduction path, this plan uses the explicitly supplied crouching case as the trigger rather than requiring all three variants in one run.

The report does not explicitly instruct the executor to enable the debug hitbox overlay. F3+B was added as a verified operational step because the reported property is an entity hitbox and the overlay allows the separate observation subsystem to inspect it directly.

The @n selector is only deterministic here if no other mannequin is nearer to the command source. The fresh-world and single-mannequin conditions are practical safeguards for preserving the supplied command without altering it.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-302466:Maps can no longer be placed in the same block as carpet | Duplicate:inward:MC-302566:Maps and item frames will break and drop if in contact with a carpet
source_meta._title: Rooms with carpet on the floor cannot have maps in item frames placed on walls touching the floor

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.21.9 Release Candidate 1, vanilla single-player Creative mode, using a new disposable world and default controls. A Superflat world is recommended only to provide a simple, level construction surface.
preconditions: Install and launch exactly Minecraft: Java Edition 1.21.9 Release Candidate 1, not the listed fix version.
Use a new disposable world so testing the release candidate cannot affect an important save.
Use Creative mode so the required blocks and items can be obtained without crafting or exploration.
Have a mouse or control binding capable of performing Use Item/Place Block; its default mouse input is right-click.
Do not use mods, plugins, or datapacks that alter item frames, maps, entity hitboxes, or block placement.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, start an installation configured for Minecraft: Java Edition 1.21.9 Release Candidate 1. Wait for the game to reach the main menu.
steps.success_cue: The Java Edition main menu is visible and its version text identifies 1.21.9 Release Candidate 1.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and create the world. A Superflat world may be selected to make the floor geometry easier to construct, but no particular seed is required.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has entered a Creative-mode world.

steps.action: Wait before building until nearby terrain has rendered and normal movement and camera input respond without world-loading pauses.
steps.success_cue: The surrounding terrain is visible and the player can move and turn normally.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab and place the following into separate hotbar slots: Stone, White Carpet, Item Frame, and Empty Map. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen.
steps.exact_input: Search terms: stone; white carpet; item frame; empty map
steps.success_cue: Stone, White Carpet, Item Frame, and Empty Map are each visible in the player's hotbar.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E. Select the Empty Map hotbar slot using its number key or the mouse wheel. Aim into open space rather than at an interactable block, then use the Empty Map once with Use Item, which is right-click by default, to create a filled map for the current area.
steps.success_cue: The selected Empty Map has become a filled Map and the map sheet can be displayed in the player's hand.

steps.action: Find a flat ground tile with an adjacent open ground tile. Select Stone and use Place Block, right-click by default, on the top of the first ground tile to place one stone block. Treat the vertical side facing the adjacent open tile as the front of the wall.
steps.success_cue: One stone block stands on the ground, with an unobstructed vertical front face and a ground tile immediately in front of that face.

steps.action: Place a second stone block directly on top of the first stone block. This makes the wall two blocks high and clearly identifies the lower wall block that touches the floor level.
steps.success_cue: A two-block-high stone wall column is present; the lower stone block is directly beside the floor tile in front of it.

steps.action: Select White Carpet. Place one carpet on top of the ground tile immediately in front of the lower stone block's front face. Do not leave a gap between the carpet tile and the wall.
steps.success_cue: White carpet covers the floor tile directly against the front of the lower wall block.

steps.action: Select Item Frame. Stand on the carpet side of the wall and aim at the vertical front face of the lower stone block, not the upper stone block. Use Place Block once to attach an empty item frame to that lower face.
steps.success_cue: An empty item frame is attached to the lower wall block, and the carpet occupies the floor-level block space directly in front of and below that frame.

steps.action: Select the filled Map created earlier. Confirm that the filled Map, rather than Empty Map, Stone, Carpet, or Item Frame, is in the active hotbar slot. The active slot is the hotbar slot surrounded by the selection outline.
steps.exact_input: Select the hotbar slot containing Map
steps.success_cue: A filled Map is held in the player's hand and the crosshair can be aimed at the center of the empty item frame.

steps.action: Aim directly at the center of the empty item frame attached to the lower wall block and press Use Item once, right-click by default, to attempt to put the filled Map into the frame. Do not click again, rotate an inserted item, remove any dropped items, or change the carpet or wall after this interaction.
steps.success_cue: The single map-insertion interaction has just been issued against the item frame sharing its floor-level space with the carpet; the scene has not been altered afterward.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just used a filled Map on the empty item frame mounted to the lower wall block directly above the carpeted floor tile. Begin observation immediately, before any additional interaction or cleanup.
uncertainties: The report contains no formal Steps to Reproduce, world seed, game mode, wall material, carpet color, or map-creation method. Creative mode, a disposable flat world, Stone, White Carpet, and a locally created filled Map are practical choices intended to preserve the reported wall/carpet/item-frame geometry without adding exploration or crafting.

The report does not explicitly state whether the failure occurs while attaching the empty frame, inserting the map, or maintaining the resulting map frame. The issue description and linked duplicate titles most strongly support using insertion of the map as the final trigger. Official Minecraft information confirms that using a map on an item frame places it in the frame and enlarges its display to a full block, while the 25w34a notes identify a map-dependent item-frame hitbox change. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-snapshot-25w34a?utm_source=openai))
A Superflat world is not asserted as required by the report; it is recommended only to simplify construction of the required floor-and-wall arrangement.

source_meta._title: Zombie nautiluses with a negative age possess a hitbox the size of a baby nautilus

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition Snapshot 25w41a; single-player integrated-server world; Creative mode; commands/cheats enabled; non-Peaceful difficulty; Overworld; open, well-lit test area; entity hitbox rendering enabled.
preconditions: Use the exact recommended affected version, Snapshot 25w41a, rather than the listed fix version.
Run an unmodified vanilla client without mods, plugins, or datapacks that alter entities, rendering, or commands.
Use a disposable test world because snapshots can damage or permanently convert worlds.
The player must have permission to execute commands; in single-player, create the world with commands/cheats enabled.
Keep the difficulty set to Easy, Normal, or Hard rather than Peaceful so the undead entity is not immediately removed.
Ensure the keyboard can issue the Java Edition F3+B debug shortcut; on some keyboards the Fn key must also be held.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, enable snapshot installations if they are hidden, create or select an installation for the exact Java Edition version 25w41a, and launch it. Do not select 1.21.11 Pre-Release 3 because that is listed as a fix version, not an affected version.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and identifies the running version as 25w41a.

steps.action: Open the Singleplayer menu and create a new disposable world. Set the game mode to Creative and ensure commands/cheats are enabled. Leave the difficulty at Normal, or select another non-Peaceful difficulty. No particular world seed is required by the report.
steps.success_cue: The world begins loading with the player configured for Creative mode and command access.

steps.action: Wait for the world to finish loading. Do not continue until nearby terrain is rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the Overworld, surrounding chunks are visible, and movement is responsive.

steps.action: Verify Creative mode by checking that the health and hunger bars are absent and the Creative inventory is available. If the world did not start in Creative mode, press T, enter the supplied mode-setting command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is in Creative mode and can fly by double-tapping the Jump control, whose default key is Space.

steps.action: Move to a clear, well-lit, level location with several blocks of unobstructed space around the player. Avoid standing against a wall, inside foliage, or beside another entity, because the supplied relative coordinates summon the zombie nautilus at the player's current position.
steps.success_cue: At least several blocks around the player are unobstructed, and there is room to back away and view the summoned entity.

steps.action: Enable Java Edition's entity hitbox display by holding F3 and pressing B once. On a keyboard whose function keys require it, hold Fn as well. Do not repeat the shortcut after the confirmation appears, because repeating it would hide the hitboxes.
steps.success_cue: The game displays a confirmation that hitboxes are shown; visible entities, if any, have white bounding-box outlines.

steps.action: Stand on the clear surface and stop moving. The report's summon command uses ~ ~ ~, so the zombie nautilus will be created at this exact current X, Y, and Z position.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary in the prepared open area with hitbox rendering still enabled.

steps.action: Press T to open the in-game chat and command input. Execute the command in-game rather than from an external dedicated-server console.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept a slash-prefixed command.

steps.action: Type the report's command exactly as supplied, including the leading slash, entity identifier, relative coordinates, braces, capitalization, comma, and negative Age value. Do not modernize, shorten, or add other NBT such as NoAI.
steps.success_cue: The complete command is present in the chat input field and has not yet been executed.

steps.action: Press Enter once to execute the summon command. This is the trigger action for the reproduction.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports a successful summon and a zombie nautilus is present at or immediately beside the player's former position.

steps.action: Without attacking, mounting, feeding, or otherwise interacting with the zombie nautilus, move approximately three to five blocks away so that the entity is no longer overlapping the camera. If necessary, use Creative flight to obtain an unobstructed side view, but remain close enough for the entity and its debug outline to render clearly.
steps.exact_input: S or another movement control; optionally double-tap Space for Creative flight
steps.success_cue: The complete zombie nautilus model is visible from a short distance and is not obscured by the player camera or nearby blocks.

steps.action: Center the camera on the summoned zombie nautilus and confirm that hitbox rendering is still active. Stop issuing commands or interactions as soon as both the entity model and its white bounding-box outline are simultaneously visible.
steps.success_cue: The zombie nautilus created with Age:-999999 and its white debug hitbox outline are simultaneously visible and ready for inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: The exact report command has been executed in Snapshot 25w41a, and the resulting zombie nautilus is visible from an unobstructed short-distance view with F3+B entity hitboxes enabled. Begin observation without interacting with or modifying the entity.
uncertainties: The report supplies only the summon command and does not specify a world seed, coordinates, dimension, game mode, difficulty, or server type. A disposable single-player Creative Overworld world with cheats enabled and a non-Peaceful difficulty is therefore used as the minimum deterministic setup.

The report does not explicitly instruct the executor to enable debug hitbox rendering. F3+B is added because the report concerns hitbox dimensions and the outline must be visible for the separate observation subsystem.

The report does not require the zombie nautilus to be summoned in water. The plan preserves the exact ~ ~ ~ coordinates and uses a clear land-based viewing area rather than adding an unsupported water requirement.

No adult or ordinary-age comparison entity is added because the supplied report requests only the negative-age summon command. Adding a comparison summon would extend the reproduction beyond the reported instructions.

source_meta._title: The hitbox of baby foxes is offset from their model when sleeping

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 26.1 Snapshot 6 in a single-player world where commands are permitted. Creative mode is a practical choice but is not stated as a bug requirement. Entity hitbox rendering must be enabled before summoning the fox.
preconditions: Install or create a Minecraft Launcher installation for Java Edition version 26.1 Snapshot 6.
Use an unmodified client without gameplay-changing mods or datapacks.
Create or load a world in which the player can execute commands; for a new single-player world, enable commands by setting Allow Cheats to ON during world creation.
Ensure the keyboard can send the F3+B debug shortcut; on keyboards where function keys control hardware features, Fn may also need to be held.
Allow the world and surrounding chunks to finish loading before beginning the reproduction.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft Java Edition using the installation configured for version 26.1 Snapshot 6, then enter a command-enabled single-player world.
steps.success_cue: The world is open in Java Edition 26.1 Snapshot 6, terrain has rendered, and player movement responds normally.

steps.action: Move to a level, unobstructed area where the ground at the player's feet is visible. Stop moving and avoid standing inside tall grass or other blocks that could obscure a small entity.
steps.success_cue: There is open ground at and immediately around the player's current position, with enough room to see a baby fox.

steps.action: Enable entity hitbox rendering by holding F3 and pressing B once. If the keyboard reserves function keys for hardware controls, hold Fn while pressing F3+B.
steps.success_cue: A debug notification indicates that hitboxes are shown. Keep hitbox rendering enabled for the rest of the reproduction.

steps.action: Aim the camera generally toward the ground at the player's feet, because the supplied relative summon coordinates place the fox at the player's current X, Y, and Z position.
steps.success_cue: The ground directly at and immediately in front of the player is visible.

steps.action: Press T, or the currently bound Open Chat control, to open the in-game chat input.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's summon command exactly as supplied, including the leading slash, and press Enter once. Do not change the entity identifier, relative coordinates, Age value, Sleeping value, capitalization, or NBT syntax.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted, chat closes, and a baby fox in a sleeping pose is summoned at or immediately beside the player's feet.

steps.action: Without attacking, using an item on, or moving away from the fox, adjust the camera downward only as much as necessary to keep the sleeping baby fox and its enabled hitbox overlay in view.
steps.success_cue: The sleeping baby fox is visible, hitbox rendering remains enabled, and no interaction has been performed that could wake or move the fox.

stor.handoff_condition: The supplied command has just summoned the sleeping baby fox, and both the fox model and enabled hitbox overlay are in view. Hand control to the observation subsystem before interacting with or moving the fox.
uncertainties: The structured Affects versions field lists 26.1 Snapshot 6. A report comment also explicitly states that the issue was reproduced in 26.1-snapshot-7, so that exact comment version string is included as an additional affected version.

The report does not specify single-player versus dedicated server, game mode, world seed, coordinates, or terrain. A command-enabled single-player Creative world and an open viewing area are practical execution choices rather than reported bug requirements.

The report supplies the summon command but does not explicitly instruct the executor to enable hitbox rendering. F3+B is added because the reported condition concerns the spatial relationship between an entity model and its hitbox.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-306267:Hardcoded forced adult behavior is inconsistent between Wandering Traders and Camel Husks
source_meta._title: Camel husks with the "Age" tag set below -24000 use their removed baby variant's hitbox size and animation speed

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 26.1 Snapshot 6. Use a single-player Creative-mode world with commands enabled, a clear flat area large enough to place two camel husks several blocks apart, and client-side debug hitbox rendering. A dedicated server and additional players are not specified or required by the report.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher can install and start the exact affected version, 26.1 Snapshot 6.
The test world permits in-game commands. The plan uses Creative mode with commands enabled as the simplest practical setup; the report does not prescribe a game mode.
Use an open, well-lit, approximately level area where two camel husks can be viewed simultaneously without nearby blocks or entities obstructing their outlines.
Use the commands exactly as supplied in the report, including the leading slash, entity identifier, capitalization of NBT tags, and numeric values.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for the affected version "26.1 Snapshot 6", then launch the game with that installation.
steps.success_cue: The Java Edition title screen is open and identifies the running version as 26.1 Snapshot 6.

steps.action: Create a single-player Creative-mode test world with commands enabled. A flat world may be used to provide an unobstructed comparison area, but no particular seed or world type is required by the report.
steps.success_cue: The player has entered a Creative-mode world in which commands can be executed.

steps.action: Wait for initial world loading to finish, then move to a clear, level area with at least six blocks of unobstructed horizontal space. Do not continue until nearby terrain is rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded, unobstructed area suitable for spawning two large entities separately.

steps.action: Enable the client debug display for entity hitboxes by holding F3 and pressing B. If the keyboard assigns media functions to the function-key row, also hold Fn as required. If hitboxes were already enabled, do not toggle them off.
steps.success_cue: The game displays the confirmation message that hitboxes are shown; subsequently spawned entities will have visible debug outlines.

steps.action: Choose the current position as the first spawn point. Ensure the player is on or immediately above solid, level ground so the summoned camel husk can settle normally.
steps.success_cue: There is open ground at the player's current position and another open location at least six blocks away.

steps.action: Press the Open Chat control, which is T by default, to open the in-game chat input.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's first command exactly, including the leading slash, and press Enter. This summons the camel husk carrying Age:-24000 and NoAI:1 at the player's current coordinates.
steps.success_cue: The command completes without a syntax or permission error, and one motionless camel husk is present at the first spawn point with its debug hitbox visible.

steps.action: Move horizontally at least six blocks away from the first camel husk while remaining in the same clear area. Do not attack, remove, or push the first camel husk. The separation is only to prevent the two hitboxes from overlapping when the second command uses relative coordinates.
steps.exact_input: W, A, S, or D as appropriate
steps.success_cue: The player is at a second open position at least six blocks from the first camel husk, and the first camel husk remains loaded and visible nearby.

steps.action: Press the Open Chat control again to prepare the second summon command.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open at the second spawn position.

steps.action: Enter the report's second command exactly, including the leading slash, and press Enter. This summons the NoAI control camel husk without an explicit Age tag at the player's current coordinates.
steps.success_cue: The command completes without a syntax or permission error, and a second motionless camel husk is present at the second spawn point with its debug hitbox visible.

steps.action: Move far enough away that the player is not inside either entity, then position the camera so both camel husks and both debug hitbox outlines are simultaneously visible. Keep track of their identities by position: the first-spawned camel husk has Age:-24000, and the second-spawned camel husk is the control without an explicit Age tag.
steps.success_cue: Two separate camel husks are visible at distinct positions, both hitbox outlines are unobstructed, and the executor can identify which entity came from each command.

stor.handoff_condition: The Age:-24000 camel husk and the control camel husk have both been summoned several blocks apart in 26.1 Snapshot 6, debug hitboxes are enabled, and both entities and their outlines are simultaneously visible. Hand control to the observation subsystem for comparison.
uncertainties: The title describes Age values "below -24000", but the report's exact reproduction command uses Age:-24000. This plan preserves the exact supplied command rather than changing the value.

The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, world type, game mode, or server environment. Single-player Creative mode with commands enabled and an open flat area are practical execution choices, not reported requirements.

The report's formal reproduction steps directly cover the hitbox comparison. A comment additionally mentions faster animation and following an adult, but the supplied commands set NoAI:1 and no separate movement or animation procedure is provided; this plan therefore does not invent an additional animation-speed test.

F3+B hitbox rendering and spatially separating the two relative-coordinate summons are operational additions needed to make the requested comparison executable; they are not stated verbatim in the report.
